tasks.spec:
You are an Elixir engineer porting one command of a Python CLI to Elixir, byte for byte. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the Cornerman repo, an Elixir/OTP port of the Ringer agent-swarm tool. Edit files here directly.

NEVER TOUCH: anything under test/ (the conformance tests are the acceptance check), DIVERGENCES.toml (the ledger of accepted differences: you may not add entries), bin/, lib/cornerman/spawn.ex, lib/cornerman/spawn/, lib/cornerman/application.ex, mix.exs, mix.lock, .git. Do not git commit, push or git add. Do not add dependencies: use Elixir's built-in JSON module for JSON and the already-declared toml_elixir (TomlElixir.decode/1) for TOML.

OWNED PATHS (the only files you may create or edit): anything under lib/cornerman/ except the Spawn files and application.ex above, plus ./notes.md. lib/cornerman/cli.ex is currently a stub that prints an error for every command; replace it.

GOAL: `bin/cornerman lint <manifest.json> [--allow-noncanonical-route]` must behave exactly like `ringer.py lint`: same exit status, same stdout, same stderr, byte for byte, except that the program name is `cornerman` where Ringer prints `ringer.py` (e.g. `cornerman: error: ...`, `usage: cornerman lint ...`, `cornerman: warning: ...`). The harness in test/support/conformance.ex runs both in one sealed environment and compares them; test/conformance/lint_test.exs lists the cases (one fixture per lint rule, manifest load errors, argv errors, engine-binary diagnostics, and every upstream template). The only accepted difference is in DIVERGENCES.toml: for invalid JSON the text after `cornerman: error: ` may be Elixir's JSON error message.

THE REFERENCE is the Python source at /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/dev/elixir/cornerman/vendor/ringer-py/ringer.py. Read these before writing code; port their behaviour exactly, including message text, finding order and edge cases:
- CLI: build_parser (line 10866, the lint subparser at ~11022) and main (11090, the lint branch at ~11136, and the error handling at its end: exceptions print `ringer.py: error: <message>` to stderr and return 2). argparse's own usage/error output for `lint` with a missing or unknown argument is also compared.
- Manifest loading and validation: TaskSpec (1725) and Manifest (1811), including every ValueError message and Python coercions such as int(...) on max_parallel and timeout_s.
- lint_manifest (1901) and every predicate it calls: spec_is_file_pointer (1989), check_cannot_fail (2005), check_may_fail_silently (2070) and its helpers, instructs_git_commit (2145) and is_negated_git_commit (2158), is_relative_expect_file, the write-collision and serial fan-out rules. Note: lint calls lint_manifest with config=None.
- Engine-binary diagnostics printed to stderr before the findings: AppConfig.load (1062/1078), load_engines (1645), built_in_codex_engine (1523), collect_engine_bin_diagnostics (1596), EngineBinDiagnostic.warning (751; note it uses Python repr() quoting), print_engine_bin_diagnostics_if_config_loads (1637). Config comes from the RINGER_CONFIG env var, else $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/ringer/config.toml, else defaults; a config that fails to load prints nothing. Where Python iterates a dict in insertion order (engines in config file order, write-collision paths), reproduce that order.
- noncanonical_route_findings (6447) and load_model_identity_registry (6371): Cornerman reads the registry from the CORNERMAN_REGISTRY env var (the harness sets it to the same file the oracle reads), defaulting to vendor/ringer-py/registry/model-identity.toml under the Cornerman root.

DESIGN: validate at the boundary. Parse the JSON and TOML, then turn them into validated structs (a manifest with tasks, an app config with engines) in one module each; lint rules then work on those structs with no error handling of their own. Keep lint rules as small pure functions. Keep Cornerman.CLI a thin dispatcher that later commands (run, ask, models) can join; main/1 returns the exit status and writes to stdout/stderr.

SETUP (run once, first, from this directory; the sandbox cannot fetch packages and this worktree has no submodule checkout):
  cp -R /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/dev/elixir/cornerman/deps ./deps
  export PATH=/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/elixir/1.20.1-otp-28/bin:/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/erlang/28.5/bin:/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/python/3.12.13/bin:$PATH HEX_OFFLINE=1 CORNERMAN_ORACLE=/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/dev/elixir/cornerman/vendor/ringer-py CORNERMAN_PYTHON=/Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/python/3.12.13/bin/python3

HOW TO RUN (after the setup, from this directory):
  MIX_ENV=test mix compile --warnings-as-errors
  mix format
  mix test test/conformance            # all lint parity cases; failures show both outputs
  mix test test/conformance/lint_test.exs:<line>   # a single case
  /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/.local/share/mise/installs/python/3.12.13/bin/python3 /Volumes/Personal/Users/davidwilliams/dev/elixir/cornerman/vendor/ringer-py/ringer.py lint <manifest>   # what the oracle prints (set RINGER_NO_SELF_UPDATE=1)
Iterate until `mix test` passes in full (the phase 0 Spawn tests must stay green). The verifying check runs outside your sandbox, with the same oracle.

OUTPUT CONTRACT: the port under lib/cornerman/, formatted, compiling with no warnings, plus ./notes.md with: your module layout and why, every Python behaviour you found surprising or had to emulate (coercions, repr quoting, ordering), the final test result line, and any conformance case you believe is wrong, with the reason. Never edit a test, the ledger or bin/ to make a case pass.
